stories.title: Claude Opus 5.5
stories.blurb: Anthropic drops Opus 5.5, the latest flagship in the Claude family — the model powering Claude Code. With 1,635 HN points and 1,000 comments, this is the week's biggest AI release for anyone in the Anthropic ecosystem. If you're building with Claude Code, this is mandatory reading.

stories.title: GPT-6 Sol and Luna
stories.blurb: OpenAI answers back with a two-model GPT-6 launch: Sol and Luna appear to target different capability/cost tradeoffs. A watershed moment in the AI arms race, arriving just hours after the Opus 5.5 announcement. Expect benchmark wars to dominate the next news cycle.

stories.title: Pentagon says overreliance on AI contributed to missile strike on Iran school
stories.blurb: A sobering Bloomberg investigation into how over-delegating lethal decisions to AI systems contributed to a catastrophic targeting error. The most important counter-narrative to this week's triumphalist AI launches — required reading for anyone thinking seriously about AI deployment.

stories.title: OpenAI GPT–6 Astra breaks Enigma message that has resisted solution since 2005
stories.blurb: GPT-6 Astra cracked a 21-year-old unsolved Enigma ciphertext, a genuine cryptanalytic feat. Whether you view it as a party trick or a landmark, it's a vivid demonstration of what frontier models can now do with historical puzzle-solving at scale.

stories.title: 'We hacked the FBI:' Hackers say they have data on all FBI employees
stories.blurb: 404 Media reports hackers claiming a full breach of FBI employee records. The implications for law enforcement operations and source protection are massive. Details are still emerging but the breach appears substantive enough to take seriously.

stories.title: Claude Code reads AGENTS.md only when telemetry is on
stories.blurb: A developer discovers that Claude Code silently skips AGENTS.md when telemetry is disabled — a significant behavior discrepancy that affects anyone who's turned off telemetry for privacy reasons. If you use Claude Code and have telemetry off, your agent configuration may not be loading. Check this now.

stories.title: SAML: A fractal of bad design
stories.blurb: Trail of Bits delivers a withering, technically precise autopsy of SAML's design failures — XML canonicalization madness, signature wrapping attacks, and more. Every .NET enterprise developer who's ever wrestled with SAML auth will feel this in their bones.

stories.title: WordPress: Unauthenticated path traversal leading to conditional RCE
stories.blurb: A critical unauthenticated path traversal bug in WordPress core can lead to remote code execution under certain conditions. If you or your clients run WordPress, patch immediately — unauthenticated RCE vectors are as bad as it gets.

stories.title: Obscura: VPN that can't log your activity
stories.blurb: Obscura is a macOS/iOS VPN built on a double-hop architecture where the two hops are operated by separate entities — meaning no single party can correlate your identity with your traffic. A privacy-first VPN designed specifically for the Apple ecosystem, with a strong technical FAQ worth reading.

stories.title: Grammarly will send unhinged messages to all your users if you try to cancel
stories.blurb: Sysadmins report that canceling a Grammarly enterprise subscription triggers mass emails to end-users — a dark-pattern hostage tactic. A cautionary tale about giving SaaS tools access to your user communication channels, and a reason to audit your vendor integrations.

stories.title: Jev introduces a new shape of LLM—System One, aka Decision Models
stories.blurb: Simon Willison's characteristically sharp take on Jev, the new 'decision model' category that outputs a float rather than text. He raises the critical concern upfront: Jev is an even deeper black box than LLMs — no reasoning trace, no explanation, just a number. Essential skeptical counterpoint to all the Jev hype this week.

stories.title: jaredpalmer/kev: tiny Jev-like family of decision models built on top of Qwen3.5 you can train and run on your own
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: ai, machinelearning, classification, model, oss, decision, engine
stories.blurb: Jared Palmer open-sources Kev: 0.8B/4B/9B decision models trained on Qwen3.5 that replicate Jev's architecture and match TypeSafe's Python SDK API. Runs on Apple Silicon (4B and 9B fit in 32 GB RAM). If you want to run Jev-style decision models locally without paying TypeSafe, start here.

stories.title: laya-mlx
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: jev, ai, decision
stories.blurb: A native MLX runtime for Laya typed decision models, clocking 7–14ms decisions on an M3 Max with no PyTorch, no text generation, no cloud API. Pure on-device structured inference for Apple Silicon. If you're building AI-powered tools on Mac, this is a remarkable piece of plumbing.

stories.title: JetBrains Air: Building a System of Products for Agentic Software Development
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: agentic, agents, ai, ide, jetbrains, ping
stories.blurb: JetBrains announces Air, their vision for agentic-first development tooling across their IDE ecosystem. As a developer working in TypeScript and .NET, this is worth watching — JetBrains has deep language intelligence and is now betting it on autonomous coding agents.

stories.title: Trying the Software factory pattern. | Irrational Exuberance
stories.blurb: Will Larson experiments with the 'software factory' pattern — orchestrating AI agents to produce software at scale like an assembly line. A grounded, engineering-management perspective on what agentic coding actually looks like in practice versus the hype. Practical reading for anyone using Claude Code.

stories.title: Thorsten Ball - What I believe about the future of software development
stories.blurb: Thorsten Ball (of Wasm interpreter fame) lays out his considered beliefs about where AI takes software development — written with the nuance of someone who actually builds things. Less hype, more craft. A grounding read amid this week's model announcement noise.

stories.title: I asked Meta's Muse for its filesystem and it sent me 6.8 GB | Mouse
stories.blurb: A researcher poked at Meta's Muse AI agent and got it to export 6.8 GB of its own runtime filesystem. A spectacular unintended data disclosure that raises immediate questions about how these agentic systems sandbox their internal state — and what else might be leaking.

stories.title: Amazon blocks Meta's Muse AI assistant in new standoff over agentic shopping • GeekWire
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: amazon, meta, muse, agentic
stories.blurb: Amazon cuts off Meta's Muse from shopping on Amazon.com, citing unauthorized access, identity spoofing, and credential capture concerns. The first major platform war over agentic AI access has arrived — and it's going to reshape how AI agents interact with web services.

stories.title: GEA — One TS codebase. MCU to iOS.
stories.blurb: GEA is a framework for writing TypeScript that compiles to both microcontroller firmware and iOS apps from a single codebase. A wild proposition that will speak directly to TypeScript developers who've ever wanted to push code all the way down to hardware without switching languages.

stories.title: Better Icon and Label Alignment
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: icon, label, css, alignment, vertical-align, font-size, icon-size, lh-unit, aspect-ratio
stories.blurb: Ahmad Shadeed digs into the surprisingly tricky problem of aligning icons with text labels in CSS — covering vertical-align, the new `lh` unit, aspect-ratio tricks, and more. The kind of precise, practical CSS deep-dive that Angular/TypeScript UI developers bookmark and return to repeatedly.
